cards.title_en: Byblos (Jbeil) Maritime Harbor & Cedar Trade
cards.explanation: Archaeological excavations and Egyptian records show Byblos (Jbeil) functioned as a premier timber-exporting port, connecting Levantine mountain forests with Nile Valley and Aegean trade routes.

cards.title_en: Myth of Isis, Osiris, and the Sacred Tree of Byblos
cards.explanation: The Greek writer Plutarch preserved a mythological story in which Isis traveled to Byblos seeking a sacred chest enclosed inside a palace cedar pillar—reflecting real trade ties between Egypt and Byblos through myth.

cards.title_en: Afqa Spring, Nahr Ibrahim, and the Seasonal Myth of Adonis
cards.explanation: Comparing myth and geology at Nahr Ibrahim shows two ways people explain nature: ancient poets linked the crimson spring water to the myth of Adonis, while geologists trace it to iron-oxide soil erosion.

cards.title_en: Sarcophagus of King Ahiram & the 22-Letter Phoenician Abjad
cards.explanation: The Ahiram sarcophagus (c. 1000 BCE) preserves one of the earliest full inscriptions in the 22-letter Phoenician consonantal alphabet (abjad), linking acrophonic signs (Aleph, Beth, Mem, Resh, Taw) to later Greek, Arabic, and Latin scripts.

cards.title_en: Writing, Recipes, and Oral Memory as a Portable Archive in the Lebanese Diaspora
cards.explanation: Just as ancient sailors carried letters across the sea, Lebanese diaspora families preserve identity through bilingual storytelling, family postcards, and shared culinary traditions.

cards.title_en: Bayt al-Hikma (House of Wisdom) & Abbasid Translation Tradition
cards.explanation: During the 9th century, Baghdad’s Bayt al-Hikma library and translation circles connected scholars of diverse faiths and languages, preserving and expanding mathematics, medicine, and astronomy.

cards.title_en: Scholars of Baghdad: Al-Khwarizmi, Al-Kindi, Hunayn ibn Ishaq, Thabit ibn Qurra & Banu Musa
cards.explanation: Baghdad’s scholarly community united al-Khwarizmi (algebra), al-Kindi (optics), Hunayn ibn Ishaq (multilingual medical translation), Thabit ibn Qurra (geometry), and the Banu Musa engineers.

cards.title_en: Contested Chronicles: Weight-in-Gold Payments & 1258 River-of-Ink Accounts
cards.explanation: Historians compare sources carefully: stories about paying translators in gold or rivers turning black with ink were written centuries later to express how precious books were.

cards.title_en: Al-Mutanabbi Street, Shabandar Café & the International Book Solidarity Archive
cards.explanation: Al-Mutanabbi Street is the historic heart of Baghdad’s literary life. When the street needed rebuilding in 2007, Iraqi booksellers and artists worldwide united to protect its book culture.

cards.title_en: Cardamom Date Kleicha, Shanasheel Courtyards & Plural Diaspora Memory
cards.explanation: Shanasheel lattice screens cool Baghdadi courtyards naturally while kleicha recipes—passed down with family variations in fillings and spices—bring relatives and neighbors together.

cards.title_en: Egyptian Fanous Lanterns & Competing Fatimid/Coptic Origin Narratives
cards.explanation: Historians compare three stories behind the Egyptian fanous: the 972 CE welcome of Caliph al-Mu’izz, Fatimid nighttime street-lighting rules, and older Egyptian lamp customs.

cards.title_en: Cairo Lantern Metalwork, Stained Glass & Khayamiya Tentmaker Appliqué
cards.explanation: Explore how Cairene metalworkers (samkari) and khayamiya tentmakers use rotational symmetry, polygons, and colour filtering to transform courtyard light.

cards.title_en: Neighborhood Soundscapes: The Musaharati Drummer & Festive Cairo Chants
cards.explanation: Cairo’s festive soundscape combines the rhythmic calls of the musaharati drummer with centuries-old lantern songs whose word origins scholars debate between Arabic and Coptic roots.

cards.title_en: Teta Samira’s Koshari & Inclusive Courtyard Hospitality
cards.explanation: Because koshari is made from grains, legumes, and spiced tomato sauce, it serves as an inclusive, plant-based dish shared across Egypt’s diverse communities.

cards.title_en: Egyptian Diaspora Celebrations & Ontario Egyptian Heritage Month Candidate Fact
cards.explanation: Community organizations in the Egyptian diaspora adapt traditional metalwork and textile crafts into safe paper-and-LED workshops during annual cultural heritage celebrations.

cards.title_en: The Traboules of Vieux Lyon and La Croix-Rousse
cards.explanation: Built during the Renaissance in Vieux Lyon and the 1800s on La Croix-Rousse hill, traboules connected workshops to river ports; today, visitors respect signs marking which passages are public.

cards.title_en: The Canuts of La Croix-Rousse & Jacquard Punch-Card Silk Weaving
cards.explanation: La Croix-Rousse buildings have extra-high ceilings and tall windows built specially for Jacquard looms, which used punched cards to program complex silk patterns over two centuries ago.

cards.title_en: Cour des Voraces, Labor Mutualism & Historical Memory in Lyon
cards.explanation: At the Cour des Voraces, architecture tells a story of community solidarity: built around 1840, its open staircase became a symbol of Lyon’s silk weavers and neighborhood mutual aid.

cards.title_en: The Mères Lyonnaises & Eugénie Brazier: Women-Led Culinary Craft
cards.explanation: Women entrepreneurs known as the Mères Lyonnaises shaped Lyon’s culinary reputation by turning home cooking techniques into celebrated restaurants and mentoring young chefs.

cards.title_en: Galette des Rois, Kitchen Brigade Teamwork & Transnational Pastry Exchange
cards.explanation: Compare how two family pastry traditions—French galette des rois and Levantine ma’amoul—use filled doughs and festive symbols to bring households together.

cards.title_en: Bibimbap (Goldongban) & Regional Variants: Jeonju, Jinju, Tongyeong & Andong
cards.explanation: Comparing Jeonju, Jinju, Tongyeong, and Andong bibimbap shows how local harvests—mountain greens, river plains, or coastal kelp—shape regional recipes and dietary adaptations.

cards.title_en: Competing Origin Narratives of Bibimbap: Ritual, Court, Agriculture & Lunar New Year
cards.explanation: Food historians compare four different origin theories for bibimbap: harvest field meals, Lunar New Year’s Eve kitchen traditions, royal court lunches, and communal holiday sharing.

cards.title_en: Obangsaek (오방색): Five-Color Cultural Symbolism & Harmony of the Bowl
cards.explanation: In Korean cultural tradition, Obangsaek connects five colours (Blue/Green, Red, Yellow, White, Black) with directions and seasons, guiding how chefs arrange ingredients in Jeonju bibimbap and Chuseok songpyeon.

cards.title_en: Jeonju Hanok Village, Giwa Roofs, Nambu Market & Pungnammun Gate
cards.explanation: Hanok architecture balances nature and comfort: curved giwa tiles shed rain into courtyard drains, raised maru floors catch summer breezes, and hanji paper screens filter soft daylight.

cards.title_en: Shared Bowls, Chuseok Songpyeon & Korean Diaspora Cultural Continuity
cards.explanation: In Korean and diaspora households, preparing Chuseok songpyeon and adapting regional bibimbap ingredients keeps family stories and language alive across generations.
